why: The chosen control drawn with the SAME border style as an unchosen one, under forced colours. This is the defect issue #368 was opened over, restored: measured in Chromium before the contract existed, `.ui-selectable`'s base `2px solid transparent` comes back OPAQUE and identical to `--on`'s authored white on both the dark and light high-contrast themes, so the ring the primitive's own comment calls "the ONLY visual signal of the current choice" disappears and every swatch, skin, source and option reads as selected. `border-color: Highlight` is deliberately LEFT in place by this mutation rather than removed with it, because colour alone is not the contract: `.hud-swatch` carries `forced-color-adjust: none` (the colour on a swatch is its content), so on a swatch the ring's colour is unforced and can land on a same-coloured Canvas -- the shape is the channel that holds in both cases. Nothing outside forced-colors mode moves, so no ordinary-rendering guard can see it, and jsdom never matches the media query at all, so no computed-style assertion can either. Killed by the text-level pair in `hud.css.test.ts` that asserts unselected is dotted, selected is solid, and the two differ. Scoped to hud.css.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only.
killedBy: forced-colors conformance (issue #368) the selected ring is distinguished by SHAPE, not only by a system colour
